claims.text: The target eutectic high-entropy alloy has dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries vulnerable to microcrack initiation during room-temperature tensile deformation.
A controlled low-temperature anneal can promote a targeted interfacial phase transformation or segregation at lamellar boundaries.
The proposed anneal will form coherent nanoscale films along the lamellar boundaries.
Coherent nanoscale interfacial films enhance cohesion at the lamellar boundaries.
The interfacial films redistribute local stress concentrations.
The interfacial films decrease susceptibility to microcrack development during tensile deformation.
Strengthened interphase boundaries delay microcrack nucleation and propagation.
Strengthened interphase boundaries improve load transfer between the constituent phases.
Improved load transfer will raise both yield strength and ultimate tensile strength relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Annealing will increase room-temperature tensile uniform elongation relative to the baseline.
The annealed alloy will show statistically significant simultaneous improvements in room-temperature tensile strength and ductility.
The baseline lamellar-colony boundaries are preferential microcrack-initiation sites that cause room-temperature brittleness.
A sufficiently low annealing temperature can avoid significant coarsening, unwanted precipitation, and alteration of the overall phase distribution.
The annealing temperature can simultaneously be high enough to activate localized atomic rearrangements at interfaces.
The strength and ductility benefits require coherent and sufficiently thin interfacial films.
Excessively thick or incoherent secondary phases, or a changed overall phase distribution, may prevent the proposed strength and ductility improvements.
Prior evidence supports interface strengthening through controlled interfacial phase formation in related alloy systems.
The precise annealing conditions and magnitude of the room-temperature ductility improvement remain undetermined.

contradictions.description: The boundary field limits the hypothesis to treatments that successfully form coherent, thin interfacial films, but the falsification rule treats failure to form those films as falsification rather than as failure to realize the specified intervention.
